_readme: Mass ledger for RMS Titanic on 14 April 1912. Displacement is a mass (weight of water displaced). Gross register tonnage is a volume measure (1 register ton = 100 cubic feet = 2.83 m^3) and must never be added to masses.

displacement_load.source: Harland & Wolff / British Inquiry: displacement at 34 ft 7 in draught

items.name: Lightship (hull, machinery, outfit)
items.estimate: commonly quoted lightweight for Olympic-class; varies 38,000-39,000 t

items.name: Coal remaining
items.estimate: 5,892 t aboard at Southampton less ~650 t/day steaming, partly offset by Cherbourg/Queenstown use

items.name: Fresh water, feed water, boiler water
items.estimate: boilers alone held ~1,500 t of water

items.name: Ballast in double bottom
items.estimate: trimming ballast in the double bottom; balances the ledger to the hull-model displacement at the observed draught

draught_observed.estimate: slightly less than load draught after coal burned

displacement_night.estimate: hydrostatics of the Port Marlowe hull model at the 10.2 m mean draught of 14 April (49,650 metric t)
